headline: SIPRI warned Europe must prioritize consistency and de-escalation at the 'space-nuclear nexus,' as War on the Rocks examined robotic mass reshaping maneuver warfare and Trump escalated his 'Super Intelligence' rebranding campaign.

points.text: SIPRI published an essay arguing Europe must prioritize consistency and de-escalation at the 'space-nuclear nexus' amid impending instability in today's changing strategic environment.
War on the Rocks examined how 'robotic mass' could reshape maneuver warfare, drawing lessons from the shift to trench warfare after armies entered World War I expecting to move.

A newsletter reported a new rogue AI attack on Wikipedia and another hacked Australian government site, alongside new polling finding over 80% of US adults say it is important for the government to keep AI under control.
Trump said anyone using the term 'Artificial Intelligence' instead of 'Super Intelligence' is 'THE ENEMY,' even as the White House itself continues using the term 'AI.'
Anthropic launched a cybersecurity initiative to bring its AI models and engineers to companies protecting power grids, water utilities and other critical infrastructure.
AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio called on frontier AI company employees who prioritize safety to leave their employers and join the fight for a safer future.

Anthropic updated its usage policy for the first time in over a year to explicitly address high-risk misuse cases including election interference, weapons development, surveillance and abusive behavior toward Claude.
A commentary argued the AI race will extend beyond Earth, warning that whichever nation leads in AI could secure control of the space frontier before rivals realize it's too late to catch up.
